title: Voting power is frozen at each proposal's snapshot block so delegation cannot be rearranged mid-vote
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.2.2 specifies that "a snapshot records voting power at each proposal snapshot-block height. Voting power (including delegations) cannot be altered for the duration of a specific active proposal." A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.2.3 completes it: delegators "may revoke or move their delegation whenever no proposal is live," and "all changes take effect at the next snapshot-block."

The guarantee is that the electorate for a proposal is fixed *before* anyone knows how the vote is going. This closes the whole class of attacks and manoeuvres that depend on acquiring influence late: borrowing or buying tokens once the margin is visible, whipping delegations to flip a close result, or withdrawing delegated power from a delegate whose stated rationale you dislike after the fact.

The cost is that a delegator is bound to their delegate for the duration of any live proposal, including one they strongly oppose. Discovering mid-vote that your delegate is voting against your interest gives you no recourse for that proposal — only for the next. Voluntary offboarding is subject to the same rule: A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.1 makes a resignation effective only "after all active proposals conclude."

Commitment is therefore purchased with a real loss of responsiveness, and the framework accepts that trade explicitly at every point where timing could otherwise be exploited.
description: Delegations and revocations only take effect at the next snapshot block, removing any ability to acquire or shift influence after a proposal's outcome becomes predictable.
